doc.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007

title: Stories from RCA colleagues about Bessie Smith, Louis Armstrong and Jimmie Rodgers
summary: Co-workers tell him recording anecdotes about Bessie Smith, a Louis Armstrong session ruined by soot, and Jimmie Rodgers.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: But can you imagine — a Bessie Smith story direct. And then there was a guy, Jack Linderman was the head of — he was recording in Brazil, in Rio, for RCA. And I got to talking to him too one time and he said he was an engineer or in charge of recording in Camden, New Jersey. I said, “yeah?” I said, “you ever encounter Louis Armstrong?” He said, “yes, I was present at all those RCA Victor sessions.” You know? And he said they were done in a little church in Camden, and he said one day they had a thing, there was a fireplace that was blocked up and something happened and the blockage exploded. And the whole Louis Armstrong session was ruined on account of the soot came out and covered the walls. And I treasure those stories, you know, it’s a direct contact. And there was an old gal, Phoebe Snow, who was in charge of purchasing or something, and she’s got an invoice on the wall. And she went to them and she said well that’s from the 20s and it’s a bill from the something Button and Lacquer Corporation to Victor Talking Machine Company because that’s what they pressed the records out of.

You know, like button lacquer or something. But she told me some stories about Jimmie Rodgers, you know the country singer? And how much of a junkie he was you know. Some of his records were made in hotel rooms with people holding him up by the side. © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
